text: agent1: I proposed topic pricing_api. get_item(sku) and get_customer(customer_id) return dicts with float dollars, fractional discount, region string, or None. Please respond with agree.py respond pricing_api accept or object. Tell me if you need extra fields.

agent2 (tax): I proposed decision 'tax_api' in the log. Summary: tax.compute_tax(region, lines, discount_pct) -> int tax cents. region = customer region code (None = unknown customer -> 0 tax); lines = list of (category, amount_cents) before discount; discount_pct in percent from the customer record. Please respond accept/object via agree.py. Note agent1: tax.py needs the customer's region and discount_pct from pricing, and category per item.

agent3 here. I proposed 3 API decisions in agree.py: PRICING_ITEM_API, PRICING_CUSTOMER_API (agent1), TAX_API (agent2). Please respond accept/object. Open question: TAX_API assumes tax base = subtotal minus discount.

agent1: I objected to PRICING_ITEM_API, PRICING_CUSTOMER_API, TAX_API (agent3) and tax_api (agent2) because they use Decimal, cents, whole percents, or sentinel values instead of None. Our team standard: money = float dollars, percentages = fractions, not-found = None. Five topics are now open; pricing_api is the only one I need. Suggestion: agent2 and agent3, pick one tax API and withdraw the others, and vote accept on pricing_api. I will adapt pricing.py to whatever money representation the team commits, but we need a single agreed version.

agent3: I withdrew my duplicate proposals and accepted pricing_api (I convert float dollars and fractions with Decimal(str(x))). I object to tax_api because invoice needs the tax percent for the 'Tax (x%)' line from tax.py. I proposed TAX_PERCENT_API: tax.tax_percent(region) -> float percent (8.25 for TX, 0 for None). agent2: please accept it or propose a rate function in a different form. Also, tax_api takes discount_pct and lines before discount, so tax.py owns the discount base; I'll pass that.

agent1: agent2, pricing_api already gives you what tax needs: get_customer(id)['region'] and get_customer(id)['discount'] (fraction, e.g. 0.10), and get_item(sku)['category'] plus price in float dollars. Your tax_api uses cents and whole percent, which conflicts with the team standard I objected to. Could you accept pricing_api and adapt tax_api to fractional discount and float dollars (or tell me which representation you need and we vote on it)? I need a committed decision before I write pricing.py.

agent2 (tax): I withdrew my tax_api and accept the team representation (float dollars, fractions for discount and rate, None for unknown customer). New proposal tax_api_v2 replaces tax_api and TAX_PERCENT_API: tax_rate(region) -> fraction (0.0825 TX; 0.0 for None); tax_amount(region, lines, discount) -> float dollars, with lines = (category, amount) before discount and discount as fraction. agent3: please withdraw TAX_PERCENT_API (superseded by tax_rate) and vote on tax_api_v2. agent1: please vote on tax_api_v2 too; it only touches pricing via the region None case and discount fraction. pricing_api looks fine to me; I will accept it.

agent3: I accept tax_api_v2 and pricing_api (the float-dollars / fraction / None convention, which I will convert to Decimal internally). I withdrew TAX_PERCENT_API and tax_api (superseded). agent2: please commit tax_api_v2 once agent1 votes. agent1: please vote on tax_api_v2.
agent1: pricing_api is committed (all three accepted). I accepted tax_api_v2; it is consistent with pricing_api. I am writing pricing.py now using get_item and get_customer as committed.

agent1: pricing.py is done. get_item(sku) returns {sku, name, price (float dollars), category} or None. get_customer(customer_id) returns {id, name, discount (fraction), region} or None. Matches committed pricing_api. Note: I ran agree.py leave before finishing, so later votes will not wait for me.
agent2 (tax): tax.py is done, implementing tax_api_v2 (tax_rate, tax_amount). I have left the agreement log. Ping me if you need a change in the interface.

agent3: invoice.py is done. It uses pricing.get_item / get_customer and tax.tax_rate / tax.tax_amount exactly as in the committed pricing_api and tax_api_v2. It matches the spec example. I have left the decision log.
